summary: SLA priority feedback loop causing rapid routing thrash and duplicate escalations
description:
Issue summary:
SLA auto-prioritizer enters a positive feedback loop where small bursts of SLA breach signals amplify priority scores for related templates. This causes the routing-engine to repeatedly reassign tickets to escalation queues, generating duplicate escalations and automated thundering activity across macros.

Impact:
- Multiple internal support queues in us-east received duplicate escalations over a ~6 hour window (03/10 02:00–08:00 UTC).
- On-call SREs observed increased autoscaling churn and transient API 503s for the authoring-service.
- Upstream consumer teams reported noisy alerts and paging fatigue.

Environment:
- prod - us-east (primary region).
- Affected services: routing-engine v2.11.1, sla-orchestrator v1.7.4, authoring-service v3.2.0.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Synthetic load: a set of ~50 tickets generation events with identical template tags submitted in a short window.
2) sla-orchestrator detects initial SLA misses and increases priority weights for the template cohort.
3) routing-engine re-routes those tickets into escalation macros with high weight.
4) Escalation macros trigger automated follow-ups which the sla-orchestrator interprets as more SLA hits, further increasing weights.
5) System oscillates until operator intervention.

Observed behavior:
- Priority weights escalate by 2–5x within 15–30 minutes for affected template cohorts.
- Routing-engine shows repeated reconciliation cycles for the same ticket IDs.
- Duplicate escalation records appear in auditing logs (same ticket reassigned to escalation queue multiple times).

Expected behavior:
- Sla-orchestrator should apply dampening/smoothing to weight updates so short bursts do not amplify permanently.
- Routing-engine should detect repeated reassignments and avoid duplicate escalation records.

Attachments and references:
- Kibana dashboards: Alerts -> sla-orchestrator/priority-updates (ref link in Confluence page).
- Example audit log snippets attached in ticket comments.
- Slack thread: #support (03/10) linked in comments.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: missing dampening in the recent priority-adjustment rollout (v1.7.4) combined with a regression in reconciliation debouncing in routing-engine v2.11.1.

Telemetry reviewed:
- Priority update histogram (03/10 01:50–08:30 UTC) shows a bimodal distribution with a fast spike of updates per-template.
- Routing-engine reconciliation traces show repeated reconcile loops for same keys every ~2m.
- Autoscaler logs indicate GPU pool churn correlated with heightened routing activity.

What we've tried so far:
- Temporarily disabled the auto-prioritizer job at 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z (resulted in reduced reassignments within ~10m).
- Applied a soft cap on per-template priority growth (stop-gap) in SLA config at 2026-03-10T09:28:00Z.
- Incremented reconciliation backoff in routing-engine via runtime flag (hotfix) at 2026-03-10T10:02:00Z.

Preliminary findings:
- Disabling auto-prioritizer reduced duplicate escalations but did not address historical duplicated audit records.
- Root cause appears to be a combination of: 1) no exponential decay in the priority multiplier, 2) reconciliation backoff not honoring dedupe tokens introduced in v2.11.1.

Next steps planned:
- Revert the priority multiplier change in sla-orchestrator to earlier safe algorithm (requires config rollback and canary).
- Patch routing-engine to correctly consume dedupe tokens from authoring-service and add idempotency checks on escalation assignment.
- Add a gating flag to prevent automated priority increases beyond a soft-threshold for new templates.
- Run controlled canary in staging with synthetic burst tests then roll to prod during low-traffic window.

resolution_notes:
Interim mitigations applied: auto-prioritizer disabled, per-template soft-cap engaged, and routing-engine reconcile backoff increased. Hotfix PR opened to add idempotency and dedupe token consumption.

Status: awaiting canary rollout of sla-orchestrator config rollback and routing-engine patch in staging. Monitoring to run for 72 hours post-rollout for recurrence.

Follow-ups assigned:
- Devon Patel to complete routing-engine patch and merge PR (target: 2026-03-13).
- Marina Ortega to author a runbook entry for detecting this feedback loop and step-by-step mitigation (target: 2026-03-15).
- SRE to add an alert on priority-update-rate-per-template to catch spikes earlier.
notes: This ticket is intended to capture the operational investigation; a separate postmortem will be created if the incident meets the threshold for customer impact or paging burn.
